analysis.title: Who's Left Holding The 'CoreWeave' Collapse Bag? Investment Advisors Quintupled AI Datacenter Bond Holdings This Year
key_insights: Goldman credit strategists (Amanda Lynam, Sara Grut, Shamshad Ali) report USD high yield AI-related spreads widened 25bps in one session between Oct 13 and 14 to a record 360bps over Treasuries. Non-AI junk widened only 2bps and remains below its March peak.

Within the AI cohort, widening is driven by datacenter project finance and AI-related corporates. AI-adjacent Energy and Utilities names barely moved, which Goldman attributes to more diversified revenue and defensive earnings.

Goldman places AI-related corporate bonds from neoclouds or firms with significant frontier lab exposure at the epicenter of the funding cost debate. Softer AI sentiment can widen datacenter bonds, especially if off-taker credit risk is reassessed.

AI-related investment grade spreads are only 3bps wider versus 1bp for non-AI IG. Oracle CDS hit a record, and Deutsche Bank warned (Oct 15) that an Oracle downgrade from BBB could trigger forced selling by IG-only investors.

Goldman reviewed Bloomberg holdings for the universe of 20 USD HY project finance bonds with $45.6B notional outstanding. $23.3B of holdings are reported. CoreWeave is the tenant on seven of the 20 bonds.

Investment advisors hold $18.2B, up from $3.7B at end-2025, roughly 5x. Insurance companies hold $2.8B, up from $0.5B. Banks, brokers and others hold small amounts. Advisors own about 78% of the reported holdings.

The average dollar price of the 20 bonds fell from $101.5 on June 30 to $94.7 on Oct 14, a loss of almost 7 points. The Bloomberg USD HY Corporate index fell from $97.1 to $93.4 (about 3.7 points) over the same period, so rates explain roughly half of the decline.
ZeroHedge's napkin math applies the 6.7% average drawdown to advisors' $18.2B for roughly $1.2B in paper losses. The estimate is rough because holders bought at different prices.

Goldman notes dispersion: 2025 and early-2026 vintages with fatter coupons and data halls close to delivery trade near or above par, while more recent issues trade in the low-to-mid $90s. The bond count rose from 4 at end-2025 to 20 now.

Goldman's Three Cs framework for datacenter project finance covers construction risk, coverage (full amortization within the lease term versus refinancing risk), and claim to hyperscaler (guaranteed lease payments, who pays power, taxes and insurance). Goldman now adds power availability, permitting, insurance and location to the checklist.

USD IG and HY project finance issuance reached $106B this year, nearly 3x the 2025 full-year total of $37B, almost all datacenters (including chip and compute financings). Average IG project finance tranche is $6.9B and HY is $2.3B.

Goldman expects $300B of global project finance issuance for datacenters and compute in 2027, on top of $420B of direct hyperscaler issuance, about $720B in total. It sees risks to the $300B figure as firmly skewed to the upside and a high bar to derailing the investment despite a higher cost of capital.

Goldman stays neutral on USD HY, sees scope for some near-term reversal of the selloff and calls valuations more attractive, and stays underweight USD IG Tech. It would be cautious of a broad, top-down move meaningfully tighter in datacenter structures given AI macro beta and technical supply overhang.

ZeroHedge's own view (not Goldman's) is that the market reprices rather than reverses, likely lower, particularly with the market again pricing a Fed hike. It also cites CoreWeave CDS pricing better-than-even odds of default (Oct 14).

Oracle CDS hit a record. Deutsche Bank warned a downgrade from BBB could trigger forced selling by IG-only investors.

risk_factors: Off-taker credit risk: seven of 20 HY datacenter bonds have CoreWeave as tenant, and its CDS is cited as pricing better-than-even default odds.
Supply overhang: $106B of project finance issued this year and $300B of project finance plus $420B of hyperscaler issuance expected in 2027.
Concentrated ownership: investment advisors hold about 78% of reported holdings, up roughly 5x since end-2025.
Oracle downgrade from BBB could force selling by IG-only investors.
Higher cost of capital and a Fed the market is pricing to hike.
Construction, coverage and hyperscaler-claim risk, plus power availability, permitting, insurance and location constraints.
vol_and_positioning: Investment advisors hold about 78% of reported holdings in the 20 USD HY datacenter project finance bonds, concentrated in a single investor type, which raises forced-selling and crowding risk.
